title: Budget cuts threaten Germany's fight against antisemitism and racism
summary: Numerous grassroots initiatives in Germany are facing funding cuts. Affected organizations are sounding the alarm, pointing to growing challenges posed by far-right extremism.

title: COP deadlock prompts calls for a reset of climate diplomacy
summary: COP31 has been branded a failure after countries couldn't reach a final agreement, divided over a reference to "fossil fuels." But was the decision to walk away from a watered-down text actually a show of strength?

title: German police respond to multiple school bomb threats
summary: Police in Germany are responding to bomb threats against a series of schools, but say that at present they don't believe them to be credible. Danish authorities are reporting a similar series of apparent hoaxes.

title: Germany news: Metalworkers go on strike as pay dispute heats up
summary: Germany's biggest union is calling for more strikes over heated pay disputes with car makers like Mercedes and shipyards among the companies impacted. Meanwhile, a Berlin hospital fire leaves many injured.

title: Germany's Early Start Pension: Can child investment accounts help?
summary: Germany plans to pay €10 a month into investment accounts for children to encourage long-term retirement saving. Economists say the measure may help build wealth but won't solve the country's pension funding challenge.

title: Gukesh to defend chess crown against rising star Sindarov
summary: As the World Chess championship gets underway, it's no coincidence that the titleholder, Gukesh Dommaraju, and his challenger, Jakhovir Sindarov, are both from Asia.

title: 'I've lost her forever' — Why German voice actors are refusing to sign Netflix's AI contract
summary: For decades, Germans have known Hollywood's biggest stars through the same familiar voices. Now an AI clause in Netflix contracts is splitting the industry over whether it protects performers or exposes them.

title: North Macedonia remains stalled on its EU path after 21 years as a candidate
summary: EU enlargement has regained momentum, with Montenegro and Albania moving closer to membership. But North Macedonia, a candidate since 2005, remains stalled by a politically difficult dispute involving Bulgaria.

title: Nvidia reinstates former CEO Jensen Huang despite China espionage scandal
summary: Nvidia's board voted unanimously to bring back the disgraced CEO, who resigned this month amid news of his affairs. He's suspected of having had a relationship with a Chinese intelligence asset.

title: Rembrandt's 'The Night Watch' is more alive than you'd expect
summary: A new project and exhibition, "The Night Watch Lives," lifts the veil on the hidden world of microbes covering one of the most famous paintings of the Dutch Golden Age.

title: Rule-breaking is contagious — and good examples barely help
summary: Seeing someone break a rule makes people more likely to break it too, a new study has found, especially when the rule-breaker is on their side politically. Watching others behave well barely made a difference.

title: Uganda minister at COP31: 'We need a just transition'
summary: Funding from wealthy countries to help deal with the impacts of climate change hasn't materialized, says Uganda's environment minister. The East African country is hoping oil and carbon credits will help boost finances.

title: US and UK to host Women's World Cups in 2031 and 2035
summary: FIFA has confirmed the United States, Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica will host the 2031 Women's World Cup — the first to feature 48 teams. The UK will stage the 2035 edition, its first World Cup since 1966.
